title: De un día para otro: un cambio repentino

sections.content: De un día para otro (overnight, from one day to the next) emphasizes how suddenly a change happened -- useful when a reading wants to stress that there was no gradual transition, just an abrupt before and after. It's an adverbial phrase that can appear at various points in a sentence. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El costo de esa deuda se disparó, de un día para otro, sin que los países hubieran hecho nada distinto.
items.english: The cost of that debt shot up, overnight, without the countries having done anything different.

items.spanish: De un día para otro, los bancos internacionales dejaron prácticamente de otorgar nuevos créditos.
items.english: Overnight, international banks practically stopped granting new loans.

items.spanish: La confianza de los inversores desapareció de un día para otro, cerrando por completo el acceso a nuevo financiamiento.
items.english: Investor confidence disappeared overnight, completely closing off access to new financing.

items.spanish: Muchas familias vieron cómo su nivel de vida cambiaba, de un día para otro, tras el estallido de la crisis.
items.english: Many families saw their standard of living change, overnight, after the crisis broke out.

sections.content: De un día para otro emphasizes suddenness the way de repente does, but works especially well with changes that unfold over the following weeks or months once triggered -- not just an instant event.
